objects.name: AuthLogEntry
objects.description: One recorded authentication event: a sign-in, a failure, a lockout, a refresh, a key use. Read through the authentication trail endpoint.

fields.name: ID
fields.description: Identifier of the entry.

fields.name: At
fields.description: When it happened, in UTC.

fields.name: Event
fields.description: What happened. One of the authentication events rig records.

fields.name: Outcome
fields.description: Whether it worked: Succeeded or Failed, and no third value.

fields.name: AccountID
fields.description: Who it happened to, absent when the attempt never resolved to an account — which is what an unknown address looks like.

fields.name: EmailAddress
fields.description: The address as presented, lowercased. Present even when no account matched.

fields.name: IPAddress
fields.description: Where the attempt came from.

fields.name: UserAgent
fields.description: What made the attempt.

fields.name: APIKeyID
fields.description: The key involved, when one was.

fields.name: APIKeyRef
fields.description: The public half of a key as presented, whether or not it resolved to one that exists.

fields.name: SessionID
fields.description: The session involved, for grouping a family's events together.

fields.name: Detail
fields.description: Whatever else was worth recording — the addresses a replayed token was used from, the administrator who ended a session.

objects.name: Error
objects.description: Returned whenever a request fails.

fields.name: Code
fields.description: Machine-readable reason the request failed.

fields.name: Message
fields.description: Human-readable explanation. Not intended for clients to parse.

fields.name: RequestID
fields.description: Identifier of this request, for correlating with server logs.

fields.name: Fields
fields.description: Present when the failure was validation. It is shaped like the request body that failed — one member per field, holding the problem with that field — so a client can put each message beside the control it belongs to.

fields.name: Without
fields.description:
Relations with no row matching the given conditions. An empty one asks for no related row at all.

This is where a negation belongs when what you mean is "not": it negates whether a matching related row exists, so a row with no related row at all satisfies it. The negative operators above negate the comparison instead and still require the related row to be there — "no related row called X" is here, "a related row not called X" is NotEquals.

fields.name: CreatedAt
fields.description: When this row was created. Set automatically and never changes.

fields.name: Account
fields.description:
Conditions on this row's Account.

A row with no Account never matches, and that holds for the negative operators too: under NotEquals this asks whether the Account is there and differs, so a row without one fails that as well. To ask the other question — no matching Account, which a row with none satisfies — use Without.Account.

fields.name: Tenant
fields.description:
Conditions on this row's Tenant.

A row with no Tenant never matches, and that holds for the negative operators too: under NotEquals this asks whether the Tenant is there and differs, so a row without one fails that as well. To ask the other question — no matching Tenant, which a row with none satisfies — use Without.Tenant.
